text: I’ll model the water directly in metres as the union of the central 16 mm sphere and three orthogonal 24 mm-diameter through-bores clipped by the 40 mm cube, then subtract the 15 mm ball. This preserves six distinct outer circular openings; the eventual boundary will be split into the ball, residual spherical hollow wall, six cylindrical bore-wall segments, and six openings. I’ll first build and render this exact fluid volume at coarse display tessellation, while measuring its bounds and volume.

The preview shows the intended connected six-port cavity and the enclosed ball boundary. The 21 CAD faces are consistent with one ball face, six bore walls, six openings, and the residual spherical hollow wall split into eight trimmed faces by the Boolean operation. I’ll inspect each face’s exact surface type, area, and representative center so patch grouping can use analytic surface identity and bore direction—not bounding-box extremum tests.

The analytic types confirm the expected topology and also show why a face-center shortcut is unsafe: trimmed cylindrical faces have parameter-space “centers” offset around their circumference. I’ll query the installed face API for the cylinder’s intrinsic axis/geometry data, which will let each bore wall be assigned from its cylinder axis and positive/negative axial span.

The intrinsic cylinder axis is available and already carries the generating half-bore direction. I’ll print those axes and planar opening normals to verify that all six signed directions are represented exactly once before exporting patches.

Each full generating cylinder retains an unsigned axis, but the trimmed face’s area centroid has a clear signed axial coordinate (about ±15.29 mm), so combining intrinsic axis direction with centroid projection distinguishes the six walls without any global bounding-box test. For the two spherical surface families, I’ll inspect the OCC adaptor to identify their exact radii rather than relying on face area.

The spherical adaptor reports exactly 16 mm for the hollow wall pieces and 15 mm for the ball, so all patch groups can now be defined from analytic surface properties. I’ll check `export_patches`’ installed signature, then export the 14 named patches in one conformal tessellation call.

I’ll name signed ports `xPlus/xMinus`, `yPlus/yMinus`, and `zPlus/zMinus`. Cylinder-wall signs come from the centroid’s projection onto the cylinder’s intrinsic principal axis; opening signs come from their exact planar normals. The ball and hollow wall are separated by their OCC sphere radii. The exporter will clear abandoned STL files in `constant/triSurface` and write one conformal STL per patch.

The conformal export is closed (0 open, flipped, or non-manifold edges) and contains all 14 requested STL patches. For meshing, I’ll use `snappyHexMesh` on a 2.5 mm Cartesian background and refine every boundary to 0.3125 mm (level 3), giving roughly three cells across the critical 1 mm water clearance. The inside point is chosen in the shell along the cube diagonal at radius 15.5 mm, away from all bore axes. I’ll now write the minimal meshing dictionaries and generate only the coarse background mesh.

The background mesh is correct at 45 mm extent with 5,832 cells and 2.5 mm spacing. I’ll now run `snappyHexMesh -overwrite`; its output will show whether the thin shell survives castellating and snapping at level 3.

`snappyHexMesh` stopped during dictionary loading before any meshing stage, so this is a setup error rather than a geometry failure. I’ll inspect the short error tail and correct only the missing or invalid dictionary entry.

The failure is only because this otherwise empty case lacks the standard `fvSchemes` file that the snapping motion solver reads. I’ll add minimal standard mesh-generation numerics plus an explicit quality dictionary (so replay does not depend on an external include path), then rerun the mesher.
The geometry loaded successfully; OpenFOAM 2512 additionally requires an explicit (possibly empty) `features` list. Since implicit feature snapping is enabled, I’ll add `features ();` and rerun.
Snapping completed with 266,332 cells and no mesher quality errors. I’ll now run the binding bare `checkMesh` and inspect its topology, geometry summary, and patch list before rendering a cutaway.

The binding check passes: one connected region, 266,332 cells, 14 non-empty named patches, maximum non-orthogonality 47.7°, skewness 2.24, and mesh volume \(2.06839\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^3}\), within 0.12% of the CAD volume. I’ll render a central clipped view of the volume mesh to visually verify the ball exclusion, thin shell, and bore connections.

The cutaway confirms the ball is excluded, the 1 mm spherical water layer is retained, and the six bores connect that layer to the six outer circular faces. No requested geometric property remains unchecked: CAD radii and cube extent were measured directly, and mesh volume was compared with CAD volume. I made one interpretation choice: each “hole” is the portion of a 12 mm-radius axis-aligned bore from its cube face to the spherical cavity; opposing holes are geometrically collinear but remain separately named by side. No advisory warning is expected, so I am not waiving any check.

The coverage advisory reports complete, exclusive coverage—14 patches over all 8,172 triangles, with every face in exactly one patch. That is the requested condition, so I’ll explicitly waive this informational warning as correct rather than alter the geometry or patching.
